name: desired-fps
title: Desired frame rate
summary: A dot that slides across a track every 2 s, in a document whose header asks the player for 30 fps.
prompt: An animated dot that slides along a track every 2 seconds, capped at 30 fps to save battery.
teaches: Cap how often an animated document repaints with header.desiredFPS
Loop a position every 2 s with (continuousSec() % 2) / 2, which also makes the player repaint every frame
Map the 0..1 phase onto a track: x = 30 + phase * 240
Paint the canvas background with a background modifier instead of a full-size drawRect

snippets.note: ask the player for 30 frames per second instead of its default

check.describe: Repaints every frame (repaint verdict continuous); at 10:00:01 the dot is mid-track (x = 150), at 10:00:00 at the left end. Resized (200×100, 450×140) the track spans the width less 30 on each side and stays vertically centred, the dot mid-track.

pitfalls: animationTime() alone never schedules a repaint: the player's getOpsToUpdate only wakes for listeners on continuousSec (every frame), timeInSec, timeInMin or a wakeIn, so a dot driven by animationTime() stays put on an idle host (the inspector reports repaint idle). Drive continuous motion with continuousSec()
Paint ops are cumulative: after a stroke paint, the next fill shape must set {"style": "fill"} again or it is drawn as an outline
desiredFPS is a hint to the player, not a timer: the motion must still come from a time expression, and speed is set by the expression, not the fps
Canvas coordinates written from the header size (a track from 30 to 270 at y 50) stay put when the host gives another box: derive them from componentWidth() / componentHeight()
